questionsToConsider: Which purchase should people answer about? Naming the product, or passing it in with the link, gives far more accurate answers.
Do you sell online, in shops or both? Trim the channel options so every choice is one a customer could really have used.
Which competitors would you like named? Leave the question open if you'd rather not put names in front of customers.
How soon after purchase will you send it, so the decision is still fresh?
guide.howToUseResponses: Lay the answers out as a sequence: trigger, first contact, research, comparison, purchase. Look for the step where the most people say information was hard to find, and fix the content there first. Read the answers about competitors and hesitation together, since they tell you what your pages need to address before a buyer has to ask.
customizeSteps: Edit the discovery and research options to match the channels you actually market on.
Add the product or order as a hidden field from your order email so the first question can be skipped or prefilled.
Send the link within a week of purchase, in the order confirmation or a follow-up email.

faqs.q: What is a path to purchase survey?
faqs.a: It asks recent buyers how they got from noticing a need to buying: what set it off, where they looked, what they compared and why they chose you.

faqs.q: When should I send a path to purchase survey?
faqs.a: Within a week or two of the purchase. After that, people remember the product better than the decision.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a path to purchase and a customer journey?
faqs.a: The path to purchase covers the steps up to buying. A customer journey also covers what happens afterwards, such as delivery, support and repeat purchases.

faqs.q: Should I ask people who didn't buy?
faqs.a: It helps, but it is a different survey. Buyers explain what worked; people who left explain what was missing.
